correctness.rationale: All n outer points remain exposed since ρ<1. The inner vertex criterion ρ cosδ>cos(π/n) is necessary by outer facet inequalities and sufficient by the nearest facet normal plus n≥m ensuring unique maximizing inner vertex. Modulo outer facet-normal period, inner phases form k=m/gcd(n,m) equally spaced sites each with multiplicity g. A uniform phase hits an interval of fractional length q at either floor(kq) or ceil(kq), with fractional probabilities, proving exact two-atom law, mean and variance. Variance zero exactly q=j/k; Taylor expansion ρ_n=1−λ(π/n)^2 proves the gcd-class critical limit. Independent literal planar monotone-chain hulls for 1000 random valid triples all matched the predicted atoms.

The exact vertex-count distribution across all orders/radii, complete deterministic threshold radii and arithmetic near-circle variance discontinuities are structurally informative, not merely a finite census or arbitrary sample.

limitations: Planar concentric polygons with n≥m≥3, 0<ρ<1, one uniform rotation, null alignment exceptions ignored.
